summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with shortness of breath, productive cough, and a history of lethargy and fever. She was found to have right middle lobe pneumonia on chest X-ray, which was later confirmed as multilobar pneumonia on CT angiography. She also had signs of a urinary tract infection, with foul-smelling and cloudy urine, and was treated with Levofloxacin and continued Bactrim. Vancomycin was initially started but discontinued due to low suspicion for MRSA. The patient improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was weaned off supplemental oxygen. She was discharged home on a short course of antibiotics and continued home oxygen therapy. Speech therapy evaluated her dysphagia and did not find aspiration risk. No procedures were performed.
